title: Feature-tier downscaling: semantic-aware pruning & graceful fallback playbook
creator: Daniel Kim
description:
Problem: During regional surges and multi-region failover events we often hit capacity limits that force blunt load-shedding decisions (drop requests or entirely switch to smaller models). These blunt actions cause disproportionate functional regressions for feature-rich requests (e.g., tool-calls, long-history summarization, multi-pass reranking) while leaving cheap requests unaffected. We need a structured, predictable way to degrade features on a per-request basis that: 1) preserves core user intent satisfaction where possible, 2) prioritizes critical tenants and SLOs, and 3) gives operators deterministic levers for rollout and rollback.

Proposal summary: Build a Feature-Tier Downscaling subsystem that combines a lightweight on-path intent classifier + feature-cost catalog + admission coordinator to progressively disable or bypass expensive features per request. The system exposes ranked feature-tiers and a graceful fallback ladder: feature-tier-0 (full feature set) -> tier-1 (disable non-essential heavy features like full-history context and large reranker) -> tier-2 (switch to quantized/smaller model variant, reduce sampling diversity) -> tier-3 (serve cached or truncated response, incrementally notify client about degraded fidelity). Tier selection is governed by SLO burn forecasts (region + tenant), circuit-breaker state, and tenant priority.

Key components:
- Intent/importance classifier: tiny model (<=10ms CPU) that tags requests as "essential", "nice-to-have", or "non-critical". Runs in the admission path before costly execution.
- Feature-cost catalog: per-feature expected extra CPU/GPU tokens and tail-latency delta based on historical traces; stored as time-series and aggregated per-region.
- Admission coordinator: central service that maintains region-level SLO budgets and per-tenant credits; decides tier for incoming requests using deterministic rules and optional ML scoring.
- Degradation adapters: pluggable gates per feature (history window, reranker, tool-calls, sampling temperature, model variant). Each adapter exposes a fast bypass mechanism and logging hook.
- Circuit-breaker integration: if downstream model endpoints or reranker services cross error/latency thresholds, feature-tier escalates automatically and routes to fallback.
- Observability + explainability: per-request annotation of chosen tier, reason codes (SLO_budget_low, tenant_credit,degraded_downstream), and signal traces for audit and post-incident analysis.

Goals & success metrics:
- Keep P99 latency regression for critical tenants under 10% during surges compared to baseline.
- Reduce total request drop rate by 60% during simulated regional overloads by using tiered degradation instead of outright 503s.
- Maintain user-facing correctness (measured via holdout prompt evals) such that degradation reduces quality in a predictable, monotonic way.

Rollout phases:
1) Simulation & offline evaluation: run feature-cost estimator and classifier on historical traces; simulate tiered decisions and measure QoE regressions.
2) Shadow mode in one region: admission coordinator makes decisions in shadow while runtime logs chosen tier for analysis and offline evals.
3) Canary enabling for low-risk tenant cohort: enable tiered downscaling in a small slice (1-2% traffic, low-RPO tenants) with strict SLO alarms.
4) Gradual ramp with playbook gating and automated rollback thresholds (p99 latency, error rate, QoE eval delta).

Operational playbooks / runbook snippets:
- Surge detected: if region SLO burn > threshold and queue occupancy > 75% then enable tier-1 globally in region and notify on-call via pager.
- Tenant over-budget: if tenant credit < 10% then mark tenant requests as tier-2 by default; provide webhook to tenant indicating degraded mode.
- Circuit-breaker trip on reranker: escalate tier for requests depending on reranker calls count; reroutes to cached or single-pass scoring.
- Emergency cutover: if cascading failures occur, admission coordinator switches all non-essential requests to tier-3, sets promotional status to "degraded-mode" and triggers post-incident run.

Trade-offs and decisions considered:
- Doing costly classification on-path adds latency; decided to use a very small classifier with confidence thresholds and fallback to heuristics when classifier times out.
- ML-based per-request scoring vs deterministic rules: initial rollout uses deterministic, explainable rules; long-term plan is to augment with ML scoring to improve sensitivity to request semantics.
- Where to store feature-cost catalog: we chose time-series (Prometheus+TSDB) with daily aggregation to ensure low-latency reads in the coordinator.

Implementation plan (high level):
- Phase A (4 wks): implement lightweight classifier prototype, feature gate adapters for history-window and reranker, offline simulation harness.
- Phase B (6 wks): admission coordinator service + SLO budget store, integration with circuit-breaker endpoints and tenant credit ledger.
- Phase C (4 wks): observability surfaces (per-route dashboard, tier distribution, QoE eval hooks), canary rollout.

Acceptance criteria:
- Shadow runs show >=50% reduction in simulated drops without violating p99 SLO for critical tenants in two weeks of traces.
- End-to-end latency overhead of classifier + admission coordinator < 12ms P95.
- Feature gates can be toggled via Console with audit logs and per-tenant overrides.

updates: 2026-03-02 - Daniel Kim: Kickoff meeting with runtime and console teams. Agreement to prototype classifier as a library to avoid cross-language rewrites.
2026-03-05 - Priya Shah: Prototype classifier v0 trained on anonymized intent labels; initial P95 classification latency ~9ms (CPU).
2026-03-08 - Performance review: team decided to default to heuristic when classifier confidence < 0.6 to avoid tail latency spikes.
2026-03-10 - Design review feedback from Alex Nguyen (SRE): add explicit tenant opt-in flag for canary and require per-tenant billing annotation when falling back to cached responses.
2026-03-11 - Security review note from Hannah Li: no sensitive data should be logged in intent labels; classifier input will be hashed and audited.
2026-03-12 - Priya Shah: Admission coordinator prototype deployed to staging; feature gate adapter for history-window implemented; running shadow traces now.
comments: Alex Nguyen (SRE): +1 to deterministic rules for initial rollout. Need stronger rollbacks for tenant SLA violations.
Priya Shah: We'll add per-tenant opt-out as part of Phase B and surface cost impact in Console.
Daniel Kim: Consider adding a small synthetic traffic generator during canary to validate behavior under controlled overloads.
Hannah Li (Security): Confirmed classifier inputs will be redacted; add automated audit to prevent PII leakage.
